<page>
 Montgomery County District Court
 Cause No. 2025-CV-0002
 William Stone, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of William Stone
Date:
December 20, 2025
Location:
Offices of Gardner & Morris Law Group
Examining attorney:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Sergio Acosta, Gardner & Morris Law Group
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, but I can confirm I'm the plaintiff in this matter.
Q: Fair enough. Let's talk about the collision. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was driving on a two-lane road in League City, Texas, heading toward a grocery store. It was a weekday afternoon and
traffic was light.
Q: What were you doing right before impact?
A: I had slowed down for a turn signal ahead. The other car came across the center line. I braked as hard as I could, but we still
collided head-on.
Q: How fast would you estimate you were going?
A: Not fast. Maybe twenty or twenty-five miles an hour. It didn't feel like a high-speed crash. The airbags did not deploy.
Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?
A: No. I didn't hit my head. I was jolted forward and then pushed back into the seat. My neck snapped, and I felt it right away.
Q: When did the neck pain begin?
A: Within a few hours, it was stiff and sore. By the next morning, the pain had spread into my shoulders and I had hedaaches at
the base of my skull.
Q: Did you seek medical care?
A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic that same evening, and then I started physical therapy about a week later. I've been going
about two or three times a week since.
Q: Are you still receiving treatment?
A: Yes. My doctor has me doing exercises at home, and I still use a heating pad most nights.
Q: How has this affected your daily routine?
A: I have trouble sleeping through the night because I can't find a comfortable position. I've had to cut back on yard work and I
stopped going to my weekend pickleball league for now. Lifting groceries out of the trunk hurts.
Q: Has anyone else been able to help with those tasks?
A: My spouse has taken on more of the cooking and cleaning. I'm trying to push through it, but some days are harder than others.
</page>
